newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand bonds rally to records after tender.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand bonds rally to records after tender.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 92.97 (PREV 92.94) 90-DAYS 7.35 (PREV 7.35)
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.75 PCT (PREV 7.60) US 5-YR 6.15 (PREV 6.16)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 761.62 (PREV 763.87) Reuters NZ MCI -63 vs -61
New Zealand bonds staged a big rally on Thursday after a well-received bond tender, with long bond yields crashing through resistance to three-year lows.
Brokers said the market was likely to charge on so long as the Reserve Bank did not voice its displeasure at how easy monetary conditions have become.
However, they said there was likely to be profit taking.
The Monetary Conditions Index remained constantly at more than 60 points easier than the RB's desired level making some traders increasingly nervous.
"The MCI is knocking on a level the RB is probably uncomfortable with. The bank may be forced to do something," said one bank's chief trader.
He said overseas players took a medium-term view and they figured there was only one way for MCI to go -- easier.
Some doubt the bank will act only four trading days ahead of the June quarter CPI data where the risk is seen on the the number being lower than forecast.
One bank chief dealer described the day's activity as a "monster day".
"People are looking for relative values and New Zealand is seen as cheap," he said.

The action was precipitated by a $300 million government bond tender where the new long bond, the 7/2009, was auctioned at 6.825 percent -- well below expectations and at the same level of the 11/06s were then trading at.
The new bond closed at 6.70 percent. The 11/06s closed 15 basis points lower on the day at 6.72 percent. There was heavy interest from overseas players and sellers were sparse.
One chief dealer said the Reserve Bank had got itself into a predicament.
"The rigidity of their policy, having and MCI the way it is, is opening themselves up. I think the hedge funds are taking them on here perhaps.
"There is still very good selling in the currency and very good buying in the bonds."
The local yield spread over U.S. treasuries has narrowed to under 50 points, seen as dangerous territory by some players.
The New Zealand market was helped by a much weaker than expected employment report in Australia which assisted a fall in long bonds there to 3-1/2 year lows.
-- Simon Louisson, Wellington newsroom, 64 4 4734 746
